Back in my day when we were growing up under Atatürk's modernization, our region experienced many changes but nothing quite like this chapter from the early republic era. It was during World War I that things took an unfortunate turn for folks of Armenian descent living around eastern Anatolia — a place close to my heart and where generations before me made their livelihoods thriving on agriculture, trade routes, you name it.

The Ottoman rule back then decided something drastic: large-scale deportation - I mean expulsion of Armenians from our homeland. Can't even begin to imagine the terror and chaos that must have caused; people uprooted without warning or choice is heartbreaking, no matter how you look at it.

Numbers tell a grim tale – hundreds upon thousands lost their lives in this exodus driven by war times’ madness but also fueled perhaps more sinister motives too complicated for simple understanding and still debated today; some say genocide was the order of that day, others not so sure. 

As a Turkish man rooted to my own country's modern narrative – our journey from Empire downfall towards Republic — I see these events as historical grievances wrapped in political disagreements between Turkey and Armenia today; it’s something we grapple with, still wrestling the past while shaping future of nation.

Our current education system should strive to teach our young ones facts without letting politics color their understanding too much – this seems like an important task for us all as citizens in a rapidly changing world where historical disputes can sometimes cloud clear communication and mutual respect among nations with shared histories, just like between Turkey and Armenia.
